messages.subject: math expression in text,ggplot2
parts:
Hi, dear all,
I have written the codes as following
[code]
rm(list=ls())
x <- c(4,1,1,6,6,2,2,5,5,6,6,3.6)
y <- c(1,1,6,6,6.8,6.8,1.2,1.2,5,5,2.5,2.5)

lbls <- c(
"list(X[1]^(0),X[2]^(0))","list(X[1]^(1),X[2]^(0))","list(X[1]^(1),X[2]^(1))",
"list(X[1]^(2),X[2]^(1))","list(X[1]^(2),X[2]^(2))","list(X[1]^(3),X[2]^(2))",
"list(X[1]^(3),X[2]^(3))","list(X[1]^(4),X[2]^(3))","list(X[1]^(4),X[2]^(4))",
"list(X[1]^(5),X[2]^(4))","list(X[1]^(5),X[2]^(5))","list(X[1]^(6),X[2]^(5))")

lbls <- paste('(',lbls,')','')
{plot(x,y,main="X vs Y",xlab=expression(X[1]^(t)),type="l",ylab=expression(X[2]^(t)),xlim = c(0,7),ylim = c(0,7))
lines(x,y,col="black",lty="dotted")
text(x-.4,y+.2,labels=parse(text=lbls),cex=0.8)}

[/code]

How could I rewrite the above codes use "ggplot2". I have try the following codes
[code]
rm(list=ls())
x <- c(4,1,1,6,6,2,2,5,5,6,6,3.6)
y <- c(1,1,6,6,6.8,6.8,1.2,1.2,5,5,2.5,2.5)

lbls <- c(
"list(X[1]^(0),X[2]^(0))","list(X[1]^(1),X[2]^(0))","list(X[1]^(1),X[2]^(1))",
"list(X[1]^(2),X[2]^(1))","list(X[1]^(2),X[2]^(2))","list(X[1]^(3),X[2]^(2))",
"list(X[1]^(3),X[2]^(3))","list(X[1]^(4),X[2]^(3))","list(X[1]^(4),X[2]^(4))",
"list(X[1]^(5),X[2]^(4))","list(X[1]^(5),X[2]^(5))","list(X[1]^(6),X[2]^(5))")

df <- data.frame(x=x,y=y)
lbls <- paste('(',lbls,')','')

p <- ggplot(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_path()
p +  annotate("text", label=expression(lbls), parse = TRUE)
[/code]

However, the above codes not work well.

Best Regards,
wanhaiyou

messages.subject: Re: math expression in text,ggplot2
parts:
Hi:

It's easier if you put the labels into the data frame. Here's what I
came up with.

DF <- data.frame(x, y, lbls, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(DF, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
theme_bw() +
geom_path() +
geom_point() +
geom_text(aes(x = x - 0.3, y = y + 0.2, label = lbls),
size = 4, parse = TRUE) +
labs(x = expression(X[1]^(t)),
y = expression(X[2]^(t)),
main = "X vs. Y") +
xlim(0, 6)


Dennis
